Supreme Court reads education access into Article 21

A three-judge bench of the Supreme Court held on 12 March 2026 that access to schooling in a Scheduled Area is inseparable from the guarantee under Article 21. The Court called the provision “a facet of the right to life” — and said the Fifth Schedule places an affirmative obligation on the Governor.

The bench read Articles 14, 19 and 21 together and declined to disturb the finding of the High Court. It recorded that the Union had allocated ₹1,200 crore to the National Tribal Health Mission in the current year, and that 62 per cent of that allocation remained unspent.

The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (NCST) had been consulted before the notification was issued. The Court noted that Section 6 of the Forest Rights Act, 2006 vests the determination of individual claims in the Gram Sabha, and that a Scheduled Area district cannot short-circuit that process.

Counsel for the State argued that the obligation is directive rather than enforceable. The bench rejected that reading, observing that a constitutional obligation does not become advisory because it is expensive to discharge.
